recipes.name: Strawberry Cake Filling
ingredients_raw: 2.5 cups frozen strawberries, thawed and cut into bite size pieces

steps.text: Whisk water and cornstarch together in a large saucepan. Stir in strawberries and sugar.
Cook over medium heat until thickened, about 10 minutes. Allow to cool completely before use.

raw_recipe.headline: Strawberry Cake Filling
raw_recipe.description: This strawberry cake filling for cakes, tarts, and pastries is easy to make on the stovetop with frozen strawberries, cornstarch, sugar, and water.

review.reviewBody: found this recipe last minute recipe and it turned out great!! thanks! i did add a squeeze of lime juice though!

Easy Peezy, and tastes great. Like many others on this site, I only used 3/4 of a cup of water. Thickened up nicely. Easily fills an eight inch cake. For those of you that use scales; a cup of strawberries is about 5.5 oz,or 152 grams. What I've found works for me. If you are filling a cake, I lay down a very thin, almost transparent layer of buttercream before I add the strawberries. This keeps them from soaking through the layers. Also used a to prevent them from squishing (that's a technical term lol) out when the next layer is added.

Loved this, used it as a King Cake filler since we are a lactose intolerant household and can't do the usual cream cheese mixes. I made it with fresh strawberries chunked up. After cooking I did put it into a blender for 2 or 3 pulses to break up the chunks of strawberries for the consistency I wanted inside the cake. It sat in the fridge overnight and came together nicely and was plenty thick enough for the cake the next morning. I added a few drops of red food coloring to get it to pop a little more, and I wanted that contrast with the white dough of the king cake. Cake out wonderful and it was the first time I had ever made a fruit filling. Will definitely be using this again for another King Cake this week.

this is a great recipe! I was crunched for time and after reading reviews that say it has to sit in the fridge, i did alter it a bit. I only added 1/2 a cup of water, and 3/4 cup of sugar. I didn't use any cornstarch, but i added 1 cup of fresh strawberries and 1/2 strained strawberry puree. I also zested and juiced an orange and a teaspoon of lemon juice. After cooking it for 25 mins I put the pot in an ice water bath for 10 minutes and it was perfect!

Made this today for a 3 layer cake (red velvet, strawberry and white) I used 4 cups strawberries, 1 cup water, 1 cup sugar and 4 tbls. cornstarch as I'm making two cakes at one time. It's amazing, not to sweet but nice and thick to put between the layers. I brought this to a boil and then simmered for almost 20 minutes for the consistency to be correct. I'll be using this for other cake fillings with different fruit.

Delicious! Added the juice of 1/3 lime and used fresh strawberries instead of frozen and crushed the berries with a potato masher type thing while cooking which made it absolutely perfect. Also made with mixed frozen berries one time and also turned out great:) If you add another tablespoon of corn starch, you can make homemade jam/jelly :)

Perfect time I make it. This time I only had 2 tble of corn starch so I added 1 tsp. tapioca. Came out perfect and taste great. Tip: I make glaze and let it thicken. I let it cool off some and then add the berries. Keeps the berries looking beautiful and the taste is great

This recipe was the “surprise treat” in my Strawberry Crunch Cake! I did tweak it just a little. I used 3TSP + 1/4 tsp of cornstarch and I added 1 tsp of lemon zest & the juice from that lemon (“waste not want not”). I let it sit in the fridge overnight, the taste & consistency was spot on!!

Meh...my first batch came out super runny so second batch I added 3 more tablespoons of cornstarch and got it to thicken up immensly. Doing a 10in round wedding cake so I needed for a filling not a topper, too runny and cake will get mushy and slide around, so 3 tablespoons extra will give you a very jelly like consistency , if you trying to use as a topping, just add 1 more tablespoon until your desired consistency.
Was in a jam. And used this recipe. Amazing, used some lemon juice, and a shot of Cartier S'Mores cream liquor.. Everyone wanted to know my secret!!

This filling turned out perfect! I used frozen strawberry halves and they broke down into pieces as I stirred it during the 10 mins of cooking time. I finished it off with squeezing in half a lemon for that extra pop of flavour, but could also do with a little bit of vanilla. Totally using this recipe again!

Followed the recipe exactly but and the taste was wonderful but the color was a light pink and didn't look appetizing. I would have added a little strawberry jello just to make the color brighter if I had any on hand. I placed it in the middle of vanilla cake and frosted with whipped cream frosting. It was delicious!! No one complained that it didn't look the best.
Very easy to make
Great yummy recipe but like everyone says use half the water
I made it just as written, it was delicious.
I used it for my black forest cake with strawberry filling instead of cherries and it was a hit!!

i used fresh strawberries and it was delicous
